implementation.reader: BufReader<File>::read_line parses only complete NDJSON lines; a record is never split across a chunk.
implementation.byte_budget: --chunk-bytes N bounds each published batch. The reader completes the current same-timestamp group before crossing the boundary, so a timestamp boundary is never cut. --chunk 0 and --chunk-bytes 0 keep the materialized reference mode for exact parity comparison.
implementation.state_preservation: Each batch uses engine.add_data(batch, None, true, true), engine.run(None, None, None, true), engine.clear_data(). Open positions, timers, pending commands, queue and funding state stay continuous. engine.end() runs once after the final batch.
implementation.funding: Funding-rate updates are pre-collected in a bounded pass and injected at their economic timestamp, including historical backfill lines that arrive at the end of a capture. This reproduces the global timestamp order used by the materialized reference without buffering economic events.
implementation.durable_purge: After each published batch the runner purges closed cache orders and closed positions (cache.purge_closed_orders / cache.purge_closed_positions) with --purge-buffer-secs. Open positions, pending commands and undelivered funding are retained by the cache guards. The funding epoch ledger releases closed epochs only after --epoch-retention-ns; settlement ids in the tape remain the auditable history.

resource_limits.max_active_orders: --max-active-orders (default 10000); exhaustion returns status RESOURCE_LIMIT with reason MAX_ACTIVE_ORDERS
resource_limits.max_epochs: --max-epochs (default 1000000) counts active plus retained closed epochs; exhaustion returns RESOURCE_LIMIT reason MAX_EPOCHS
resource_limits.max_pending_fundings: --max-pending-fundings (default 100000); exhaustion is an explicit RESOURCE_LIMIT error
resource_limits.failure_contract: RESOURCE_LIMIT emits partial_tape=true and no MARK/END_FOLD. The runner does not force-flatten, skip economic events, or silently drop records; the receipt reports the processed prefix and the observed value.

implementation.rss_sampling: --rss-samples PATH writes one JSON line per published batch with VmRSS, VmHWM, active orders/positions, retained epochs and purge counters.
